definitions.explanation: The country in northwestern Europe. The name comes from Portuguese "Holanda". During the Edo period the Dutch were the only Europeans allowed to trade with Japan, through the island of Dejima in Nagasaki, so Western learning reached Japan in Dutch as {蘭学|らんがく} (Dutch studies).

examples.japanese: オランダ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{風車|ふうしゃ}→風車：17008_fuusha⟧。
オランダ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦チューリップ→チューリップ：05487_chuurippu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{有名|ゆうめい}→有名：01106_yuumei⟧だ。
examples.english: The Netherlands is famous for tulips.

examples.japanese: ⟦{江戸|えど}{時代|じだい}→江戸時代：20431_edojidai⟧、⟦{長崎|ながさき}→長崎：30731_nagasaki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{出島|でじま}で⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧オランダ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{貿易|ぼうえき}→貿易：01727_boueki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{続|つづ}けられて⟦いた→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: In the Edo period, trade with the Netherlands continued on Dejima in Nagasaki.

notes:
The kanji abbreviation is {蘭|らん}, seen in {蘭学|らんがく} (Western learning through Dutch books) and in {日蘭|にちらん} (Japan-Netherlands). Several everyday Japanese words came from Dutch in this period, such as ⟦ガラス→ガラス：01777_garasu⟧ (glass), ⟦コーヒー→コーヒー：00789_koohii⟧ (coffee) and ⟦ランドセル→ランドセル：11191_randoseru⟧ (school backpack).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- オランダ{人|じん}: a Dutch person
- オランダ⟦{語|ご}→〜語：09841_go⟧: the Dutch language
- オランダ⟦{料理|りょうり}→料理：01523_ryouri⟧: Dutch cooking

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japan the country is still usually called オランダ, though its official Japanese name is オランダ{王国|おうこく} (Kingdom of the Netherlands). The Nagasaki theme park ハウステンボス recreates a Dutch town.
